item.title: Blue Populist Democrats Have One Target: Breaking Up Big Tech
item.description: The blue wave that swept over the US on November 3rd was so big that it’s easy to be carried away with statistics. But even more important than the size of the sweep is the changing nature of the party that achieved it. This Democratic Party is not merely a continuation of the one defined by Bill and Hillary Clinton, Barak Obama and Joe Biden. But nor is it an extension of the Democratic Socialism of Bernie Sanders, Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez and the rest.
item.dc:creator: Adrian Wooldridge

item.title: Target-Date Funds May Hold Too Few Stocks for Retirees
item.description: This may not be the right time to ask if Americans need more equity in their retirement portfolios. But the retirement industry has never been good at market timing.
item.dc:creator: Allison Schrager

item.title: Capita's UK Pension Mess Shows Why Government Outsourcing Is a Mistake
item.description: Capita Plc lost three-quarters of its market value after replacing its chief executive officer amid a botched takeover of the UK’s Civil Service Pension Scheme. Who could possibly have seen this coming? Only everybody who remembers Carillion Plc, the outsourcing giant that collapsed in 2018 leaving a trail of chaos in its wake.
item.dc:creator: Matthew Brooker

item.title: High Inflation Puts Fed’s Credibility on the Line
item.description: As US consumers are all too aware, rising prices remain a persistent problem. If the Federal Reserve wants investors to believe its promise to get inflation back down to its 2% target, it’ll have to raise interest rates next month. The question is by how much.
item.dc:creator: The Editors

item.title: UniCredit-Commerzbank: Andrea Orcel Wins Big in Berlin After Italian Loss
item.description: Andrea Orcel has just managed to obtain in Germany what he couldn’t get at home. The 63-year-old banker has scored his biggest M&A success to date as UniCredit SpA’s boss: He cleared the last regulatory hurdle to take control of Commerzbank AG and is set to be installed as the lender’s chairman.
item.dc:creator: Tommaso Ebhardt

item.title: The US Is Squandering Its Lead Over China in Aerospace
item.description: Amid the controversy over whether Nvidia Corp. chips were diverted to China, a House committee has raised another delicate technology-transfer problem that has been going on for years: US and allied aerospace companies helping Beijing advance its production of civilian and military aircraft.
item.dc:creator: Thomas Black

item.title: Burnham Is Planning an Election Manifesto in Disguise for the UK
item.description: It has been more than four months since Andy Burnham marched down triumphantly from England’s North to seize No. 10 Downing Street, but he somehow remains reasonably popular with voters. This is an achievement given the British public’s lack of patience. Five months in, Keir Starmer polled at -29. Gordon Brown was -23, and Boris Johnson -20.
item.dc:creator: Mihir Sharma

item.title: QR Codes in Dubai Restaurants Prompts Viral Rant and Serious Thoughts
item.description: The restaurant scene in Dubai probably has more QR codes per capita than anywhere else in the world. It’s not just a hangover from Covid. Downloading a menu to your smartphone in a language you can read is probably more convenient and efficient for cooks and servers who have to deal with a region full of poly-national expatriates. item.dc:creator: Howard Chua-Eoan

item.title: China’s Drones Are Reshaping Asia’s Militaries
item.description: Southeast Asian militaries have a modernization problem: They cannot afford to miss the global shift toward drone warfare, particularly after Ukraine demonstrated the importance of cheap unmanned systems and rapid adaptation. And yet some of the most affordable and readily available technology comes from China — and buying it risks creating a dependency that could bring its own dangers.
item.dc:creator: Ruth Pollard

item.title: Japan's Nidec Shows Succession Is Important at Founder-Led Firms
item.description: A charismatic billionaire, accused of running the company he founded like a personal fiefdom, returns as chief executive officer amid investor alarm over a slide in the stock price. The firm has no succession plan, and the board concludes it can’t prepare for life without its visionary leader.
item.dc:creator: Gearoid Reidy

item.title: Morgan Stanley Has An Edge With Anthropic’s New Millionaires
item.description: Anthropic PBC’s shares are floundering after its near-$120 billion stock sale last week, but thousands of its staff are still suddenly richer than they ever dreamed. They now face an army of financial advisers desperate to become Best Friends Forever. Those from Morgan Stanley likely have a head start.
item.dc:creator: Paul J. Davies
